> 隨。元亨，利貞，無咎。

The seventeenth hexagram is about following, and the character is so plain that it refuses to carry a moral.

## 隨 is 從辵，隋聲

說文: 隨，從也。從辵，隋聲.

Phonetic compound; 辵 relates it to walking. The original sense is simply: to follow.

Not "to be bound." Not "to choose the right leader." Those are readings the hexagram supplies afterward.

The character itself says only: going along with. Whether the going-along is right is the whole business of the chapter, and the word declines to pre-judge it.

## 官有渝

Line 1: 官有渝，貞吉.

官: 說文 官，吏事君也 — the office, the charge; here, what one is responsible for, the standing rule of one's post.

渝: to change.

So the first line says: what you are charged with can change with the time, and that is correct.

Which is an unusual opening for a chapter on following. Before following anyone, the thing you are holding can be revised. (An alternate text has 館 for 官; "what is held changes" is the reading this book takes.)

And the same line adds 出門交有功 — go out the gate and meet; there is accomplishment.

The gate, again, as in 同人. Following that stays inside the gate is not following.

## 系小子，失丈夫 / 系丈夫，失小子

系: to tie, to bind, to attach.

Lines 2 and 3 state the same structure twice, with the terms swapped: tie the small one and lose the great one; tie the great one and lose the small one.

Which is the hexagram's central and least comfortable claim: attachment is not additive. Choosing a thing to follow costs you another thing, always, and the text states the cost as a fact rather than a warning.

## 隨有獲，貞凶

Line 4: following, and getting something for it — and correct, and 凶.

The line is one of the hardest in the book. 隨有獲 is not a mistake. It is following and profiting by it, and the verdict is still 凶.

And then the correction in the same line: 有孚在道，以明，何咎 — if there is trust, and it is on the way, and it is clear, what fault is there.

So the fault is not in the gain. It is in what the gain does to the following: at some point the follower is no longer following the thing, but the return.

## 拘系之，乃從維之

Top line: 拘系之，乃從維之。王用亨于西山.

拘 is to confine, to bind. 維: 說文 維，車蓋維也 — the cord of a carriage canopy, thence a rope.

Bound with ropes and then tied with cords: forced compliance.

Which the hexagram places at the very top — the far end of following. Followed by 王用亨于西山, a sacrifice. The coerced following ends in a rite, which is the most precise way to say that the form survived and the thing itself did not.

## 向晦入宴息

The 象: 君子以嚮晦入宴息.

晦 is dusk; 宴息 is rest.

At dusk, the noble goes in and rests.

The entire regulation of the hexagram is drawn from one day's rhythm: there is a time to move and a time to stop, and following correctly means following the hour, not the leader.

## The test

Take whatever you are currently following — a company, a school of thought, a person. Ask what you gave up to attach to it (the hexagram says something was given up), and then ask whether what you are now pursuing is the thing or the return from it. Line 4 is where those two separate, and it separates quietly.
